subject: Acme POC — inference migration architecture review & ops runbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Parker <olivia.parker@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme POC — inference migration architecture review & ops runbook

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for the time on Friday — excited to kick off the migration PoC. As discussed, the next step is a technical deep-dive / architecture review so we can align on migration approach (live cutover vs. gradual canary), runtime sizing, and the ops runbook we will use for the handoff.

Proposed agenda (30–45m):
- Current setup recap (provider, instance sizes, typical seq lengths)
- Target architecture & tradeoffs (dedicated vs. private deployment options)
- KV cache / prefix caching considerations and cold-start strategy
- Batching & latency SLOs — how to preserve p95 targets during migration
- Canary & rollback plan + telemetry hooks (traces/metrics)
- Pre-migration checklist & ops runbook items

Proposed slots next week (all PST):
- Tue 2026-11-17 10:00–10:45 PT (18:00–18:45 UTC)
- Wed 2026-11-18 08:00–08:45 PT (16:00–16:45 UTC)
- Thu 2026-11-19 11:00–11:45 PT (19:00–19:45 UTC)

Please let me know which one works for the Acme team and who will join from your side (networking, security, SRE). If you can share a short run-rate/profile (QPS, average tokens, peak windows) ahead of the call that will help our runtime sizing exercise.

I can include a short ops runbook draft and the network checklist as attachments for review.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-poc-runbook-v1.pdf, acme-network-checklist.xlsx

From: Olivia Parker <olivia.parker@acme-robotics.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Olivia,
> 
> Thanks again for the time on Friday — excited to kick off the migration PoC. As discussed, the next step is a technical deep-dive / architecture review so we can align on migration approach ...

Thanks Jonas — apologies, we have a leadership review moved into the Tue/Thu window for next week. I can do the Wed 2026-11-18 slot but only later in the afternoon our time. Two Qs: can we shift to 16:00 UTC (which is 08:00 PT for you) and can we include our CloudOps lead (Ben Chu) and our security lead (Tara Singh) on the call? They need to confirm network/firewall changes and any vendor access policies.

Also, we can provide a short traffic profile by EOD Tuesday (QPS and token distribution).

Olivia
Director of Product
Acme Robotics

P.S. Ben — looping you in to confirm availability for Wed 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC.

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC — inference migration architecture review & ops runbook

Thanks for the quick reply, Olivia — Wed 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC works for us.

Dev will join for runtime sizing and pre-check items. I'll attach the ops runbook draft and our network checklist for ACME to review before the meeting (brief, page per topic). Prior to the call please share: model size (parameters / checkpoint), whether the model is quantized today, avg seq length and 95th percentile, and an IP allowlist if you prefer limited access during the PoC.

Pre-call plan:
- 15m pre-check with our infra team (Dev + Ben) at 15:30 UTC / 07:30 PT — quick verification of VPC peering options and port lists
- 45m architecture review at 16:00 UTC
- Follow-up doc with canary & rollback steps and acceptance criteria within 24h

Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments (referenced): redwood-poc-runbook-v1.pdf, acme-network-checklist.xlsx

Hi all,

Confirmed — I just sent a calendar invite for Wed 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC (15:30 UTC pre-check for infra). Invite link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-poc-20261118-utc

Attachments included in the invite: redwood-poc-runbook-v1.pdf (ops runbook draft), acme-network-checklist.xlsx (network tasks). We will run the pre-check at 15:30 UTC to validate VPC/port access, and Dev will run a brief sizing exercise against the profile you shared.
